I01: 1/2
- Criterion 1 (ties the error to this argument): Met. The answer names the jump from one inspection in ten finding a violation to one restaurant in ten having one.
- Criterion 2 (says why the inference fails): Not met. The answer notes that each restaurant was inspected four times, but it draws the conclusion in the wrong direction. It says the share of restaurants could be lower than one in ten. In fact at least 100 restaurants (one in ten) must account for 400 failed inspections, so the share could be as high as four in ten but cannot be lower than one in ten. It never says the failures could be spread across more restaurants.
- Tip: Test the direction by asking how many restaurants could have produced 400 failed inspections at four inspections each, then state the range (at least 100, up to 400).
